resources.string: Ferventio
the contact listed on the distribution page for this build
1. Who processes data
This policy applies to Ferventio mobile clients. Build operator: %1$s. Privacy contact: %2$s.
Ferventio does not create a separate public profile. When you sign in, this installation is associated with the Twitch account you authorize through the configured Ferventio Server.
2. Data on your device
The app may store channels, preferences, drafts, mentions, filtering rules, scroll state, image caches, and chat history including authors, badges, message fragments, and moderation state.
Backend session credentials, the device secret, and the current Twitch access token are stored in the iOS Keychain. The Twitch refresh token is kept only by the configured Ferventio Server.

Backend session credentials, the device secret, and the current Twitch access token are protected with Android secure storage backed by Android Keystore. The Twitch refresh token is kept only by the configured Ferventio Server.
Backend session credentials and device-bound secrets are kept in platform secure storage when available. The Twitch refresh token is kept only by the configured Ferventio Server.
This build does not enable automatic crash-report uploads by Ferventio.
This build keeps redacted crash reports locally and exports them only when you explicitly choose to share them.
This build may send sanitized crash information, app/build version, and technical device or operating-system information to Firebase Crashlytics.
Crash-reporting behavior depends on the current platform and distribution configuration.
3. Network data and purpose

To read chat, send messages, moderate channels, and load Twitch metadata, Ferventio communicates with Twitch APIs and real-time services such as Helix and EventSub. Twitch receives ordinary request metadata such as your IP address.

For emotes, badges, and additional public metadata, Ferventio may contact BTTV, FrankerFaceZ, 7TV, IVR.fi, and their content-delivery networks. Those providers receive ordinary network request metadata.

If notifications are enabled, the iOS app receives a device token from Apple Push Notification service (APNs) and may register that token with the configured Ferventio Server together with the installation identity needed for delivery.
If notifications are enabled, this Android build may receive an FCM token and register it with the configured Ferventio Server together with the installation identity needed for delivery.
This build may receive notifications through an authenticated embedded socket instead of a third-party mobile push provider.
This build does not register a mobile push token with the Ferventio Server.
Push delivery depends on the current platform, build variant, and server configuration.

When settings synchronization is used, versioned settings data is sent to the configured Ferventio Server. The server also processes installation identity, device-bound credentials, push registration data, access-token leases, and security or audit metadata required to operate the service.
4. Sharing with third parties
Ferventio does not sell personal data, does not display advertising, and does not use an advertising identifier for ad targeting.

Data is sent only to services needed for the features you use, including Twitch, the configured Ferventio Server, emote or metadata providers, and the platform push provider when notifications are enabled.
In builds that enable Firebase Crashlytics, sanitized crash and technical diagnostic data may also be sent to Google Firebase.
Files you explicitly export or share are handed to the app or storage provider you choose; further processing is governed by that provider.
5. Retention and protection

Local history follows the retention limits you configure. Caches, history, preferences, and other local app data remain on the device until removed by Ferventio, by you, or by normal platform storage lifecycle behavior.

The default production Ferventio Server endpoint uses HTTPS. Custom server operators are responsible for configuring encrypted transport. Authentication secrets are kept in platform secure storage, and credential-shaped values are excluded or redacted from user-facing diagnostics where diagnostics exist.

Retention of server-side settings snapshots, audit records, and backups is determined by the operator of the configured Ferventio Server. You should review the published policy from that server operator.
6. Your controls

You can sign out, revoke the current device, or revoke all server sessions for the Twitch account. Revoking all sessions removes server-side auth sessions, credentials, push registrations, and pending deliveries for that account.

Signing out or revoking sessions does not automatically delete local channels, history, drafts, or preferences. Local data remains until you remove it separately or the platform removes stored app data.
For access, correction, or deletion of data held by the configured Ferventio Server, contact its operator using: %1$s.
7. Policy changes
Effective date: %1$s. Material changes should update both the in-app text and any published web version of this policy.
